title: Gangtok Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Gangtok hotel or homestay sells beds, food and experiences, and converts them to cash daily; the asset is the building, the cash is in the booking calendar.** Revenue arrives from room nights, F&B and packages sold through tour operators and, increasingly, homestay networks. Costs are largely fixed (staff, power, maintenance, lease or EMI) while demand is seasonal, so the working-capital cycle is short on collections but lumpy on occupancy. **Capex is the risk: a new block or renovation is paid upfront and recovered over years of room nights.**

## What has changed now
**The state is actively building the trade channel: the first Sikkim Travel and Tourism Fair runs 21-22 November 2026 at Ridge Park, Gangtok, with B2B sessions, destination presentations and confirmed participation from Yeti Airlines, Nepal, and tourism boards of Nepal and Bhutan [1][2].** Organisers have not announced expected visitor or delegate numbers, and no official guest list is out yet [2]. **That is a demand-creation event, not proof of bookings; treat it as a lead indicator only.** Peer results are strong but national, not local: ITC Hotels Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,054 crore, up 26 percent, EBITDA Rs 337 crore, up 37 percent [4]; Leela's Q2 growth was 30 percent RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led [6]; Ventive's international occupancy was 71 percent for the quarter [5]. **These tell us pricing power exists in the sector, not that Gangtok rates are rising.** Rating reports are undated and generic on hotel methodology [8][9][10][11]; use them for structure, not for Gangtok numbers.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue homestay operators and small mid-market hotels that already have repeat tour-operator business and can show a booking register.** The fair's focus on homestays, rural and community tourism, wellness and emerging destinations [1][2] points to exactly these borrowers. **Avoid first-time developers, single-property owners funding greenfield capex, and restaurants with no verified footfall history.** When a proposal lands, check the last two seasons' occupancy and average room rate from the register; if the borrower cannot produce it, collect from customer.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the season, not the year: size the EMI to the lean months, not the peak.** Take monthly occupancy, cash collection and booking-advance statements every month; if advances fall for two consecutive months, ask for the operator pipeline. **Covenant on debt-service cover and on keeping the property insured and maintained.** For homestays, insist on a personal guarantee and a lien on bookings routed through the platform.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for falling advance bookings, rising staff attrition, delayed statutory dues and any request to fund renovation out of working capital.** If the November fair produces no signed trade contracts by January, treat the pipeline as unproven. **Local sources say little about Gangtok-specific demand, so lean on first principles and the peer pricing trend [4][5][6].**
